title: narumi ensemble target, execution origin and safe error provenance
$comment: Draft public target/origin/error shapes. Artifact generation observations and publication lineage are defined separately in processing_artifacts.json.

processing_target_ref.description: The run/node/call currently inspected or confirmed by the caller. This is not a historical execution-origin reference.

processing_origin_ref.description: Historical execution identity and non-secret authorization provenance from the saved attempt. Preserve its original run, connection revision and model when a later run reuses or inspects that attempt. Never rewrite it to the current selection.

processing_current_selection.description: Current planned selection for the target node, distinct from historical origin. It is a display projection, not a substitute for full ModelSelection/config authorization checks.

processing_retry_attempt_summary.description: One public attempt observation in a retry lineage. The private retry_of edge is deliberately omitted; typed storage proves that every item after index 0 directly retries the immediately preceding attempt.

processing_retry_lineage.description: Closed confirmed-retry ancestry. attempt_chain[0].attempt equals origin_unknown and has outcome=unknown. Every item i>0 directly retries item i-1 in private durable retry_of state; retry edges are intentionally absent from this public projection. The schema permits at most one succeeded outcome, requires none when resolved_by is null and exactly one when resolved_by is non-null. Typed/server validation additionally enforces unique attempt IDs, the direct private edge chain, origin_unknown equality, and that the sole success is the final chain item whose attempt equals resolved_by. A retry may use a different connection, but the original unknown and every intermediate origin remain unchanged. maxItems=64 is the lifetime limit for this same content-unknown barrier, separate from each run's 64-attempt budget. Reject attempt 65 without consuming proof, reserving run budget or sending; preserve the existing unknown and chain.

processing_safe_error.description: Closed error assembled only from the enumerated local reason and its exact code/message mapping. provider_generation_failed may preserve any public contract error code while still replacing the upstream message. Never include upstream bodies, arbitrary provider diagnostics, secrets, raw requests or paths.

retry_attempts_used.description: Lifetime attempts already recorded for this same content-unknown ancestry, including its origin. Distinct from the current run budget.

retry_attempt_limit.description: Lifetime limit for this same content-unknown ancestry, independent of attempt_limit for the current run.

minutes_outcome_unknown_details.description: Typed ensemble unknown-call recovery state. One unresolved content_fingerprint has exactly one durable public target and exactly one public blocked record. blocked_attempt_id is the durable barrier cursor for the unknown ancestry; target is the current run/node/call that will receive the explicit retransmission and need not belong to the cursor attempt's run; latest_attempt_outcome is the cursor attempt's current durable state. The four-ID proof is the current target's run_id/node_id/call_id plus the cursor blocked_attempt_id. origin is the first unknown attempt and may belong to an older run. Typed/server validation requires the barrier key, cursor attempt receipt, cursor call and target node to carry the same content fingerprint, and requires every attempt exposed later through its retry lineage to retain that fingerprint. attempts_used/attempt_limit are the current run budget; retry_attempts_used/retry_attempt_limit are the separate lifetime budget for this same content-unknown ancestry. The cursor can be a known failure while the earlier unknown barrier remains unresolved. Full current config and the exact target/blocked receipt must be rechecked before consuming one minutes_retry confirmation. Changing the target alone never consumes confirmation proof, reserves an attempt or sends provider data. At the lifetime limit, reject before proof consumption, run reservation or send and preserve the barrier. Do not infer service-side processing or billing stopped.
